title: A wall of water
text: Radiation is energy that can harm living things. Water, ice, and Mars soil can help shield a crew, but cannot stop every particle.
question: What helps shield the crew?

title: Hello, Earth… are you there?
text: Radio waves take about 3–22 minutes to get from Earth to Mars. Point the dish toward Earth or a relay satellite.
question: Why does Earth answer late?
answers: Radio waves need time to travel

title: A tiny garden, a big job
text: Plants need light, water, and warmth. Mars soil has harmful salts called perchlorates; our game simplifies soil treatment to washing it.
question: Can we plant straight into untreated Mars soil?
answers: Yes, it is just like Earth

title: A dusty blanket
text: Dust blocks sunlight from solar panels. On Mars, wind sometimes cleared dust from rover panels and helped their power recover.
question: What helps a dusty panel make more power?

title: Air from another world
text: Ice melts into water. NASA’s MOXIE made oxygen from Mars’s carbon dioxide air; our combined machine needs electricity for both jobs.
question: What did MOXIE make oxygen from?

title: Space changes plants, too
text: In OSD-658, scientists exposed small plants to simulated space radiation and studied their gene activity. This helps them investigate how space affects future crops.
question: Why study plants and radiation?
answers: To learn how space affects crops
source: NASA OSDR · OSD-658 · laboratory study, not Mars-grown plants
